editorial_changes.before: For neural applications fix $L,m,d$ and the canonical forward model
editorial_changes.after:
For neural applications let $L$ be the hidden depth, $m$ the number of
samples, $d$ the input dimension and $n$ the hidden width. Fix $L,m,d$
and data $x_a\in\mathbb R^d$, $y_a\in\mathbb R$, $1\le a\le m$.
The first weight matrix $W^{(1)}$ has shape $n\times d$, hidden
matrices $W^{(\ell)}$ have shape $n\times n$ for $2\le\ell\le L$,
and the stored readout $W^{(L+1)}$ has length $n$. The data Gram is
$G_{ab}=x_a^Tx_b/d$, without whitening or a nonsingularity requirement.
